findings.title: New idempotency_key parameter not passed from webhook
findings.body: The webhook in `ledger/webhooks.py` calls `record_payment` with only two positional arguments (`order_id` and `amount_cents`), but the new signature requires an `idempotency_key`. This will raise a `TypeError` at runtime when the webhook triggers. Pass the idempotency key from the event data to `record_payment`.

findings.title: Payment.create called with idempotency_key but not used in save
findings.body: `Payment.create` now accepts an `idempotency_key`, but the `save` function in `ledger/store.py` does not persist this field. The idempotency key is effectively ignored after creation, breaking the intended idempotency behavior. Update `save` to store the `idempotency_key` in the database.

summary.problem: The idempotency feature is partially implemented: the function signature and early-exit logic are updated, but the webhook caller and storage layer are not aligned, risking runtime errors and lost idempotency guarantees.
summary.done_well: The idempotency check is implemented with a clean early-exit and the new parameter is added to the function signature.
